newsitem.title: ITALY: OLYMPICS-ITALY BACKS ROME'S 2004 SUMMER GAMES BID.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-ITALY BACKS ROME'S 2004 SUMMER GAMES BID.

text.p: Italian politicians told the International Olympic Committee's evaluation commission on Thursday that the entire country was behind Rome's bid to host the 2004 Summer Olympics.
"Italy, which hosted the Olympics many years ago, is ready to do it again...," Prime Minister Romano Prodi said. "We think we have everything in order."
He spoke at a meeting between Italy's top politicians and the commission hosted by President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro.
"You have before you a country which has made a very clear decision," Prodi said.
Rome Mayor Francesco Rutelli told the commission: "We have been working seriously and passionately for a long time to realise this dream."
Rome, hosts of the 1960 Summer Olympics, has 10 rivals bidding for the Games -- Cape Town, Buenos Aires, Istanbul, Lille, Rio de Janeiro, San Juan, Stockholm, Sevilla, Athens and St Petersburg.
The IOC evaluation commission has already visited St Petersburg, Stockholm, Lille and Seville.
A short-list of four or five cities will be selected at the end of March or beginning of April and the winner announced in September.
